name: OpenTofu
summary: An open-source infrastructure-as-code engine that evaluates configuration, installs providers, builds a resource graph, plans changes against state, and applies the selected operations.

features.name: Declarative resource graph
features.description: OpenTofu builds a graph of configured resources and dependencies and can parallelize operations that do not depend on one another.
benefits: Makes ordering and independent work explicit
Allows declarative infrastructure to be evaluated as a dependency structure
costs: Cycles and incomplete dependencies prevent a valid execution order
Graph behavior can be difficult to infer from large configurations

features.name: Provider extension boundary
features.description: OpenTofu obtains provider implementations through configurable installation sources, keeping provider-specific resource behavior outside the core CLI and graph engine.
benefits: Extends infrastructure management to external and custom services
Separates core orchestration from provider implementation
costs: Provider versions, installation, schemas, and credentials affect reproducibility
Provider behavior remains an external execution boundary

features.name: Plan, apply, and state lifecycle
features.description: OpenTofu produces an execution plan for proposed infrastructure changes, applies selected changes, and persists resource state used by later operations.
benefits: Provides a reviewable intermediate change set
Retains resource identity and observed values across runs
costs: State requires protection, locking, and compatible evolution
Unknown values and remote drift complicate reconciliation

mathematical_views.question: When does a configuration and its provider-backed resources admit a valid parallel execution order?
assumptions: Resources and data operations are graph nodes
References and explicit dependencies are ordering edges
Provider side effects are abstracted behind node operations

mathematical_views.question: How do configuration, prior state, provider observations, and an execution plan determine a proposed infrastructure transition?
assumptions: State and provider observations are sufficiently comparable
Unknown and sensitive values follow engine evaluation rules
Remote API transaction semantics are abstracted

costs: Graph construction and cycle diagnosis add complexity
State security, drift, and locking are operational obligations
